headline_marked: [[Google takes Dreambeans to India]] with AI-generated personal stories in 13 local languages
headline: Google takes Dreambeans to India with AI-generated personal stories in 13 local languages
summary: Google's experimental AI app, Dreambeans, expands to India, offering personalized visual stories from user data in 13 local languages, aiming for a broader audience.
details: Google has launched its experimental AI app, Dreambeans, in India, marking its first market expansion outside the U.S. The app now supports 13 local languages, including Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, and Bengali, alongside English.

Dreambeans proactively generates personalized, illustrated stories about users' interests and daily lives, drawing information from connected Google services like Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube. It recently added animated images using Google's Veo video-generation model.

India was chosen as Dreambeans' first international market due to strong user interest and the widespread use of Google services in the country. This launch follows less than two months after the app became available to all eligible U.S. users aged 18 and older.

The app recorded nearly 55,000 downloads in the U.S. since its June debut, with a significant drop in October. While its download numbers are lower than general-purpose AI apps like ChatGPT, Dreambeans focuses specifically on personalized story generation.

A potential limitation in India is that users can only select one language at a time for their generated stories, despite the app drawing on information in multiple languages. This could affect its appeal in a country where users often mix languages like Hinglish.

Dreambeans' reliance on personal data from Google accounts raises privacy questions. Google states users can choose which services to connect, disconnect them at any time, and delete their Dreambeans data from within the app.

Information deleted from underlying connected services is also removed from Dreambeans' personalization system. Users can instruct the app to avoid certain subjects, and it is exclusively available to personal Gmail account holders, not enterprise users.

The app's proactive approach carries the risk of surfacing upsetting memories, such as stories involving deceased individuals. Google acknowledges this and offers controls, similar to Google Photos, allowing users to limit which memories appear.

topic: android 17 qpr2 third-party app store requirement
headline_marked: [[Google's Registered App Stores program]] requires Android 17 QPR2 for full functionality
headline: Google's Registered App Stores program requires Android 17 QPR2 for full functionality
summary: The program, launching December 1, 2026, grants third-party stores Play Store-like privileges, but only a small fraction of devices currently run the required Android 17 QPR2.
details: Google has updated guidelines for its Registered App Stores program, which aims to give third-party Android storefronts similar privileges to the Play Store. This initiative officially launches on December 1, 2026, and will require Android 17 QPR2 or higher.

The program was initially announced in March 2026, driven by antitrust pressures, including a settlement with Epic Games and the EU's Digital Markets Act. It allows developers to register their storefronts with Google for approval.

Approved stores can offer their apps and services outside the Play Store with fewer restrictions, including using their own billing systems. Google will still oversee security standards for these registered stores and their applications.

Key features for registered app stores include one-tap installation without extra confirmation screens and automatic background app updates. This provides a smoother user experience compared to traditional sideloaded apps.

However, the requirement for Android 17 QPR2 means that only a very small percentage of Android devices, primarily supported Google Pixel models, will be compatible at launch. Many OEMs are currently on Android 17 QPR1.

Currently, only about 1% of Android devices run Android 17, though this number is expected to grow. Verified storefronts will be available in select countries, including Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, and the UK.

In the US, Google already allows rival third-party stores, like the Epic Store, to distribute directly within the Play Store as part of court settlement remedies. No app stores have been approved yet, but Aptoide, Amazon App Store, and Epic Games Store are expected to apply.
